question_type: Absolute difference of coefficients of variation of log growth rates for two debt-holder series (pinned issue, fiscal-year rows)

opus_path.decision: Issue pinned to Sept 2000 (no vintage choice); five fiscal-year-end levels 1995-1999 give four year-to-year log growth rates per series; CV = population SD / mean; answer = |CV_gov - CV_public| to 3 decimals; 'nominal' = use table values as printed.

Grepped the pinned issue for the question's own phrases ('held by the public', 'Government accounts') and found the Table FD-1 'Summary of Federal Debt' header whose columns read 'Government accounts > Public debt securities (5)' and 'The public > Public debt securities (8)', an exact wording match.
Took FD-1 col (5) and col (8), fiscal-year rows 1995-1999 (not the monthly 1999-Sept duplicate); checked column alignment with identities col4 = col5+col6, col7 = col8+col9, col2 = col5+col8.
Considered and rejected OFS-1: its 'Held by private investors' column excludes Federal Reserve holdings so it is not 'held by the public', and the OCR columns are misaligned.
numpy log-diff, population SD (ddof=0) / mean per series, absolute difference.

Sensitivity analysis showed that agency-inclusive totals, simple growth or sample SD each change the answer materially, because the public series' mean log growth is near zero and CV is very sensitive to it; the question's wording pins the chosen variant. The reviewer re-read FD-1 and recomputed independently.

opus_key_moves: Searched the pinned issue for the question's exact noun phrase and took the table whose column header matches it verbatim (FD-1 'The public > Public debt securities')
Explicitly rejected OFS-1 'Held by private investors' because it excludes Federal Reserve holdings, so it is a different series from 'held by the public'
Checked column alignment with an identity: the two chosen columns sum to FD-1's public-debt total

right_arms_note: none: at [14] it ran an FTS search for the question's literal phrase 'public debt securities held by the public' restricted to the pinned Sept 2000 file, followed the hit to FD-1 [18]-[19] and chose cols 5 and 8 at [20]; a principled, phrase-driven table choice with no adapter context. Both adapted arms instead started from a table name (OFS-1) they already had in mind.
text_vs_mechanism: Mostly a mechanism problem. The prompt arm had a correct FD-1 pointer in text and was steered away by a partly matching OFS-1 lesson; the cards arm had FD-1 on screen and skipped it. A phrase-to-header search tool plus a label-match check would have fixed both, as the no-adapter arm shows; the later card C039 shows the text fix is learnable but depends on matching the right trigger words.
notes: Adapter context can hurt: the richest context (prompt, 180 KB) led the actor to name a table before looking at the corpus, while the bare arm searched the question's own words and was right. Harness implication: make 'search the question's noun phrases in the pinned issue' a mandatory first locate step before adapter hints can name a table. The cards arm also shows that a components-sum-to-total identity can pass for the wrong concept, so series-identity checks must compare labels, not just arithmetic. The near-zero mean growth of the public series makes the CV very sensitive, so any series substitution produces a >25% error.
